content.rendered:
Fine dining, but not as you know it.

If you love the quality of fine dining but prefer a more relaxed approach to eating, then this one’s for you.

Introducing Trillium.

Located on Snow Hill Queensway (just off Colmore Row), Trillium is a modern British restaurant bringing together some of Brum’s leading experts to deliver a fine dining restaurant with a more casual approach.

Trillium is an exciting collaboration between some of Brum’s biggest names who have been on the indie dining scene for years, bringing a truly unrivalled combined wealth of knowledge and experience. The brainchild of Phil Innes (the man behind the multi-award winning Loki Wine) and acclaimed local chef Glynn Purnell (a true Brummie legend), with Rob Palmer at the helm as head chef – this really a superhero team-up of epic proportions.

Together they posed the question: why should refined food be served in a way that limits how you enjoy it? So they set out to create a restaurant combining the quality of food, drinks and service comparable to traditional fine dining restaurants, but without the restrictions of a tasting menu. A space where dishes can be shared, passed across the table and the overall feel is more relaxed without compromising on quality. The result of this idea is Trillium.

The menu at Trillium is built around dishes designed for sharing, with the idea that they’ll be enjoyed across the table (but of course you can just order your favourites for yourself). The cooking is refined, not formal, with bold flavours, seasonal ingredients and a balance between precision and comfort. No unnecessary flair, just excellent cooking and fantastic ingredients, served in a way that’s both luxurious and familiar. Menus change regularly, led by the seasons and passions of the chefs.

With Loki’s Phil Innes on board, it comes as no surprise that this is also a wine-led restaurant, with just as much focus and attention on the wine list as there is on the delicious food. The list features over 500 wines, including classic regions, lesser-known producers and plenty of hidden gems. Trillium also offers one of the most extensive by-the-glass selections in the region and is one of only two Birmingham venues awarded two glasses in the Coravin Guide. For non-wine drinkers there is of course a selection of other excellent drinks options including cocktails, spirits, soft drinks and beers.

With an ideal central location (literally a few steps away from Snow Hill Station), this is a convenient place to gather, meet and share delicious food and drinks with friends, family or whomever you choose. The space itself is classy, elegant and refined but without ever being stuffy or pretentious. It lovingly combines everything we love about premium restaurants whilst maintaining an air of casual, relaxed dining – something we need plenty more of in this city.

Since opening in 2025, Trillium have been given glowing reviews in The Guardian, The Telegraph and The Daily Mail, as well as collecting a core group of repeat customers who keep coming back for more. To see for yourself what all the fuss is about, be sure to book a table and go and enjoy one of the best meals in Brum.

content.rendered:
When those foodie cravings hit – we have the answer.

Introducing Saint Paul’s Market.

Located on Mary Ann Street, Jewellery Quarter, Saint Paul’s Market is the food hall where all your foodie dreams come true.

This foodie paradise is your must visit whenever you need to satisfy your ultimate foodie cravings, where all of your favourite independent traders can be found under one roof and you can taste your way around the world without ever leaving your seat.

With 7 kitchens (all run by local Brum independents at the top of their game), 2 bars, 500 seats set across 2 floors, and a big shiny disco ball, this is the place to go for all occasions, big or small. Whether you want a quick bite to eat after work, a long and leisurely catch up with friends over some ridiculously tasty food, or to celebrate a special milestone with loved ones, this place truly has something for everyone – when those foodie cravings hit, Saint Paul’s Market is your answer.

Bringing something brand new and exciting to Brum, this huge, epic food hall is an awesome collaboration between ourselves (Independent Birmingham) and our good friends from Baltic Market (a well established, super-awesome food hall in Liverpool) as well as the legends from Buddha Belly. This venue is our love letter to the city, and to the independents we have championed for over 13 years – bringing together some of the very best restaurants from across the city and placing them all under one roof for your convenience. A place for foodies, created by foodies.

Speaking of convenience, Saint Paul’s Market has a super easy ordering system whereby you simply scan the QR code on your table and from there you can browse the menus from all of the traders, add your desired dishes and drinks to the basket and then checkout – the rest is done for you, so you can sit back and relax whilst the kitchens prep your food and our friendly staff will bring your dishes directly to you at your table. No queuing, which means more time for socialising, chatting and enjoying yourself, safe in the knowledge your mouth-watering feast is on its way to you. However if you prefer, you can also browse the menus next to each trader and order directly from the kitchens or bar – the choice is yours!

Come and sink your teeth into mouth-watering Persian dishes cooked over fire from Colbeh, incredible BBQ Thai small plates and curries made using authentic family recipes from Soi (the team behind Buddha Belly), glorious bao (including the super popular BBQ char siu bao that you all went wild for at our Independent Birmingham Festivals over the years) and Asian-inspired small plates from Tiger Bites Pig, juicy fried chicken (and those epic beignets with fudge sauce) from Chancer’s, Detroit-style deep dish pizzas and tasty sides from Corner Shop and vibrant, street-food style Indian dishes from Zindiya. LA-POP are on desserts with their customisable gelato lollies, indulgent cheesecake pops, cookies, cakes and more, and they have some warming hot drinks and milkshakes available too. Saint Paul’s Market is a true celebration of the very best of Brum’s indie scene.

At the bar you’ll find a wide selection of super tasty drinks: from house-crafted cocktails (featuring spirits from local distillery: Spirit of Birmingham) and non-alcoholic serves, to plenty of local craft beers on tap and by the can from Brum’s best indie breweries, as well as firm favourites like Guinness. We also offer a selection of wines, including some by local producers Midland Press, and lots of spirits too if you fancy a rum and Coke or shots, shots, shots. Plus, there are plenty of soft drinks, and low and no-alcohol options too – so whatever drink you’re in the mood for, we have you covered.

The building itself is a stunning 10,000 sqft former industrial warehouse, and we’ve made sure to keep lots of the details intact whilst breathing new life into this beautiful old building. Look out for the original brickwork and the cranes, juxtaposed with our disco ball and beautiful new kitchens and bars – the result is a welcoming space filled with character, both old and new. Oh, and we have a photobooth too – perfect for capturing a special memory from your visit.

If you’re yet to visit Saint Paul’s Market, make sure to head down to the Jewellery Quarter and discover your new favourite foodie hangout today. We can’t wait to welcome you.

content.rendered:
We need to talk Barbecue.

No, we don’t mean a classic British BBQ of burnt sausages, supermarket burgers and corn on the cob, we’re talking proper American-style barbecue. Something it’s not always easy to find in Birmingham. But don’t worry, we know a spot…

Introducing TEA’s Smokehouse.

Located on the Coventry Road, Solihull, TEA’s Smokehouse is the place to go for the ultimate American BBQ feast.

When you think barbecue what comes to mind? If you’re imagining a drizzly summer day with sausages cremated to within an inch of their life as someone holds an umbrella over the dying coals, you wouldn’t be alone. But allow us to introduce you to a whole different type of barbecue. We’re talking American style, Southern BBQ – burnt ends, brisket, juicy meats lovingly smoked low and slow overnight, homemade sausages, and more.

If this sounds like the dream, then TEA’s Smokehouse is the place for you. Taking inspiration from classic Texan BBQ food, they serve all manner of mouth-watering smoked meats, barbecue platters, traditional sides, and more.

TEA’s owner started smoking meats back in 2020 as a bit of a passion project, being unable to find classic American BBQ food locally. Following some encouragement from friends and family who all loved his food, he decided to take the plunge and set up a business selling his BBQ food, beginning with set menus posted on social media (and sold out within 2 hours each time). After saving up, he and his wife finally managed to open their own business in early 2026. Now, paying homage to Texan BBQ and creating a welcoming, family-friendly environment, they’re aiming to recreate the experience you would find in these restaurants across the pond.

Everything currently on the menu is made in-house, all halal, and they smoke their food using only oak wood in their 500 gallon offset smoker (purchased from America). Their menu is packed full of mouth-watering mains like Brisket, Beef Ribs, Beef Cheeks, Burnt Ends, Pulled Beef and Chicken Wings, with classic sides like Cornbread, Coleslaw, BBQ Beans and Fries. Grab your favourites or opt for one of their sharing platters (for 2 or 4 people) to try a little bit of all of everything.

As well as all of the delicious, slow-cooked BBQ dishes, they offer a selection of classic American desserts to end your meal with something sweet. Choose from dishes like Peach Cobbler (a staple in BBQ joints across the South) or Banana Pudding, or just go for some cooling ice cream if you prefer. If you really want to lean into the authentic BBQ experience then grab yourself an Iced Tea to drink, or go one better with a Cola Float (Cola topped with a scoop of ice cream). But, of course there are other soft drinks available too.

The space itself is relaxed and laid-back, a great casual dining spot to enjoy some truly delicious BBQ food, and great for families too. If you’re in the mood for a BBQ feast then head on down to TEA’s.

Now offering Independent Birmingham App Members: a FREE side + drink when you order one or more dishes from the mains section (valid anytime)

content.rendered:
Birmingham’s love affair with Italian food is clear to see. If you’re on the look out for a tasty new Italian restaurant to visit, we have just the place for you…

Introducing Spingere.

Located on Islington Row Middleway, Spingere is a neighbourhood restaurant bringing a taste of Italy to Edgbaston.

Spingere is a wonderful independent restaurant which focuses on all forms of Italian cuisine, with a particular emphasis on authentic Northern and Central Italian dishes, including those often overlooked. As well as serving classic pizza and pasta dishes, cooked and served how they are in Italy, this lovely little restaurant also serves dishes that incorporate a twist from the owners’ Asian background too.

The restaurant was founded on the site previously occupied by the beloved Laghi’s, by one of their former chefs. Drawing inspiration from the years of experience gleaned from working at Laghi’s (as well as other Italian restaurants), they kept true to the site’s previous heritage of Italian cooking, and you’ll find some favourite dishes from past Laghi’s menus on the specials board occasionally too.

On the menu at Spingere you’ll find a selection of mouth-watering Antipasti, fresh pasta dishes, delicious mains and sides, and tempting desserts. With pasta dishes like Tagliatelle with Lamb Ragu, Gnocchi with wild garlic pesto and semi-dried tomatoes and Caserecce with nduja and gorgonzola, there are lots of bold flavours on the menu.

Mains such as Porchetta with fennel puree, and demi-glacee, Aubergine Parmigiana, or Market Fish of the Day offer a delicious and comforting take on authentic Italian dishes, and of course there are lots of tasty Antipasti dishes to start your feast the right way including Beef Carpaccio, Bruschetta, Calamari, and more.

Alongisde their core menu, you’ll also find a selection of Weekend Specials which change every week, inspired by the fresh produce and seasonal items they can find in local markets. Vegetables are sourced from their own farm in Solihull, and fish and seafood are bought fresh, directly from the wholesale markets.

If you’re in the mood for a pizza, then good news – Spingere do pizzas too! With a selection of delicious Italian toppings to choose from, including everything from a classic Margherita to Mortadella, Creamy Burrata and Pistachio, or Seasonal Vegetables, there’s something for all tastes. Finish off your Italian feast with a classic dessert including Tiramisu, Panna Cotta or a scoop or two of gelato.

On the drinks menu, you’ll find a selection of wines, beers and soft drinks as well as everyone’s favourote Italian tipple – a good spritz! Whether you go for a classic Aperol Spritz or a Limoncello Spritz, you can’t go wrong with one of these refreshing cocktails.

The space itself is laid-back and relaxed, the perfect place to enjoy a leisurely lunch sipping on a spritz or a long, lazy dinner sharing a bottle of wine. If you’re yet to visit, then plan an Italian feast now and book your table.

Now offering Independent Birmingham App Members: 50% off food when you book a table at 5pm, 6pm or 7pm (diners must order one drink + two courses to redeem) OR 20% off food (anytime)

content.rendered:
We love small plates.

Introducing Txikiteo.

Located on Frederick Street, Txikiteo is the Spanish-inspired, coal-fired small plates bar from the team behind the legendary Tiger Bites Pig, Trentina and The Church.

With a team behind them that have delivered some of the most popular casual eats venues in the city, you know this place is a winner. Inspired by all things Spanish (and in particular Basque cooking), this brilliant place is all about the flavours. And just like with their other venues, the focus here is on maximum flavours and quality cooking, making sure that every item that leaves the kitchen is utterly delicious.

Txikiteo is a Basque word which loosely means ‘going from bar to bar, having small glasses of wine and pintxos’. It’s a big part of Basque culture and cuisine and often the group will all contribute to a ‘bote’ – a central pot of money before going out, that is used to fund the evening. We love this idea, it sounds like our kind of socialising!

Naturally, the focus is on Spanish (particularly Basque) flavours but with their own spin on it, taking those traditional dishes and elevating them to new heights. On the menu you’ll find a selection of both small and large plates, all inspired by Spanish flavours. Aperitivos include Maldon Rock Oyster served with spicy Basque Chistorra sausage, Jamon Iberico and Gordal Olives – the perfect nibbles to enjoy with a drink at the bar before you move on to the main feast.

The menu is split into different sections. The flatbreads (pretty self-explanatory) come with a choice of either romesco, goats cheese and spring onion, or caramelised onion, olive and anchovy. The other sections are the Pequenos (small plates) and the Grandes (large plates). Everything is designed for sharing so you can try as many of the dishes as you can handle, and we recommend trying as many as you can because they’re all mouth-watering. Pequenos include classics like perfectly charred and blistered padron peppers, new potatoes with mojo verde (like patatas bravas but better), and Escalivada (traditional Catalan dish of roasted vegetables) as well as grilled meats like quarter chicken with mojo roja or duck leg with a refreshing fennel and orange salad.

Larger plates include Spanish-style Arroz – a rice dish with a rich base of tomato, saffron and sweet paprika with a choice of seafood (clams and shell-on Rosso prawns), roasted chicken thigh and seared duck breast, or marinated globe artichoke and roasted fennel. Other large plates include a mouth-watering pork chop with PX sauce (a glossy, sherry sauce) and a beautifully grilled Chuleton (rib-eye) with chimichurri.

For dessert, you must try their signature Basque cheesecake. These beauties have been having a bit of a moment in the last few years, but the Txikiteo folks really know how to pull it off. Soft, light and creamy, this is the perfect end to your Basque feast. Other desserts might include Sangria poached pears and Tarta di Santiago (a traditional Spanish almond cake).

To accompany your Spanish feast, they have a wonderful selection of carefully-chosen Spanish wines too. The wine menu is packed with red, white, rose, orange and sparkling wines from all across different wine growing regions of Spain. If you’re unsure what to choose, the friendly staff will help you out with their recommendations. If you’re not into wine, don’t worry their drinks selection also includes a selection of Spanish beers, Sangria and Spanish-inspired cocktails. There really is something for everyone on this menu.

On top of all the delicious food and drinks, they have a little deli section too where you can pick up some provisions. They stock all sorts of continental goodies like crisps, olives, beers and wines, so you can stock up on some tasty treats next time you’re passing by (or even pick up something to gift to a friend). The interior of the bar is very laid-back, the perfect place for a casual date night, drinks and nibbles with friends, or any occasion when great food and delicious drinks is required (basically every single day right?).

If you’re yet to visit, make sure to stop by Txikiteo for some ridiculously tasty Spanish style bites.

Now offering Independent Birmingham Members: 50% off food when you book a table on Wednesday (valid for up to 6 people – excluding grande dishes) + a FREE cheesecake when you spend £20 or more (Thursday – Saturday)

content.rendered:
Some food trends come and go, but it would seem that our love affair with Japanese cuisine is here to stay.

Ramen, in particular doesn’t seem to be going anywhere, anytime soon, with more and more places offering delicious bowl food popping up all the time. But when that ramen craving strikes, we know just where to go.

Introducing Maneki Ramen.

Located on Ludgate Hill (just off Saint Paul’s Square), Maneki Ramen, is your one-stop ramen shop when only the best bowl of noodles will do.

Having started out with a successful restaurant in Worcester, Maneki Ramen opened up their Birmingham restaurant in 2024 to much acclaim, quickly becoming one of the most popular ramen spots in the city. Thanks to chef Pete’s experience working in Tokyo, the Japanese dishes are a mix of authentic and original, with big bold flavours that will have you coming back again and again for another bowl.

This Tokyo-inspired ramen shop, naturally serves ramen (well duh), but they also serve other Japanese-influenced dishes too. Serving modern interpretations of Japanese noodle bowls and snacks, their menu is packed full of flavourful, satisfying dishes that will delight you with every mouthful. Expect bold broths, juicy rice lager, crispy Katsu and more – the kind of food that has you slurping away and sighing in satisfaction.

On their menu they have a range of snacks and small plates (think Japanese fried chicken, wings, dumplings, rice crackers, kimchi and more), and some large plates such as Katsu curry (chicken or tofu) and Yaki Soba (duck or tofu), as well as their main offering of ramen. Choose from a selection of different ramen flavours, made with different broths and meats/proteins and then customise to your liking by adding extra toppings if you like, and the option to make any bowl spicy if you’re craving some heat. They also offer the option of a smaller bowl for kids (or adults with small appetites). Whichever option you choose you’re in for a delicious, flavourful meal.

They offer desserts too, for those with a sweet tooth so look out for Japanese-inspired sweet options like matcha cheesecakes, dark chocolate mousse or miso custard caramel tart. Made with just as much love and packed with just as much flavour as the mains, this is the perfect way to end your meal.

Drinks-wise, they have everything you could possibly want from soft drinks to cocktails, beers and wines, teas and of course sake. Whether you’re sipping a delicious Japanese-inspired cocktail or a comforting tea, there’s something for everyone.

The interior of the restaurant is a fusion of Tokyo street style and Jewellery Quarter heritage, with clean lines and minimal décor giving a chic but laid-back feel to the space. Whether you’re perched around the chef’s counter watching the magic happen or cosied up in a corner with your favourite person, you’ll feel equally at home and relaxed in this beautiful, welcoming space.

If you’re yet to visit, then make sure to stop by (they take bookings but always have walk-in space available too) and cosy up with a steaming bowl of ramen – you might just discover your new comfort food space.

Now offering Independent Birmingham App members: 25% off food (valid for up to 4 people: excluding the Omakase menu + dine-in only)

This deal excludes key dates (i.e. Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, Valentine’s Day etc)

content.rendered:
We have a new favourite word: Cinnabuffin.

Fun to say, fun to eat. This is our new favourite treat (we’re poets, and heck yes we know it). If you know what we’re talking about, you’re part of the exclusive inner circle who have discovered this delicious baked good. If you don’t know what we’re talking about, then read on and be prepared to be welcomed into said inner circle. Let us introduce you to the home of the Cinnabuffin.

Introducing Pause.

Located on Poplar Road, Kings Heath, Pause is the brilliant coffee shop inviting you to take a break.

We all lead busy lives, and if there’s one lesson worth remembering it’s that slowing down and taking a break isn’t a bad thing. Whilst we’re often itching to move onto the next milestone and fill every waking moment with plans, it’s always worth remembering that we don’t need to live our lives at a million miles an hour, 24/7. With this in mind, Pause are inviting you (yes, YOU) to take a moment to pause, slow down, take a break. And in a stunning twist of fate, this little coffee shop is THE perfect place to do it!

“BUT WHAT ABOUT THE CINABUFFINS?!”, we hear you yell. Well, we won’t keep you in suspense any longer. Oh, the Cinnabuffin. A heavenly cross between Cinnamon Bun and Muffin, and brain child of co-owner and star baker, Farah. A cinnamony, sticky, sweet (but not too sweet), flaky, twisty knot of baked goodness. We don’t think there are enough words in the dictionary to describe the beauty of this delicious treat, there’s only one way to truly understand the deliciousness and that is to go try one for yourself.

Really we could write this whole article as an ode to our new favourite sweet treat, but there is SO much more to Pause than the Cinnabuffin (although it is one of their signature bakes and with good reason – believe the hype people! Ok, we’ve gone off topic again already, they’re just so damn tasty and we can’t stop thinking or writing about them…).

Like any great coffee shop, they serve amazing coffee (we’re talking interesting and rare coffees sourced from the UK’s finest speciality coffee roasters, think: Fire And Flow, Hundred House, Crankhouse, Cloud Picker, River City Roasters, and more). Co-owner Rory is the barista behind the delicious coffees, and if (like us) you’ve scoured Birmingham’s brilliant coffee shops in search of the essential brain juice, you will have more than likely bumped into Rory at some point. A fountain of coffee-related knowledge and one of the friendliest people we’ve ever met, he makes an incredible cup of the good stuff. Whatever type of coffee is your favourite, you’ll find it at Pause. Not to mention, delicious hot chocolates, matchas, teas and more. The passion and dedication this little team have to striving for excellence really shines through in the overall quality of every single drink, bake and friendly smile.

The lovely Farah doesn’t just make Cinnabuffins – she’s baker-in-chief (a very prestigious title) for a reason. Cakes, traybakes, brownies, cupcakes, cookies, whoopie pies, focaccia – you name it, she can bake it. Pop in for delicious, freshly baked goods and discover a new favourite each and every time.

Since it first opened, this coffee shop has been making waves throughout South Birmimgham and beyond, thanks in part to the amazing quality of coffee and treats available, but also because Rory and Farah are genuinely two of the loveliest humans around. If you’re yet to discover Pause, you NEED to go right that wrong immediately and discover the glorious Cinnabuffin for yourself. All hail the Cinnabuffin!

Now offering Independent Birmingham Members: Cinnamon roll + filter coffee for just £7

content.rendered:
Love wings? We know just the place for you!

Introducing Ted’s Wings & Dogs.

Located within Stir, on Pershore Road, Stirchley, Ted’s Wings & Dogs is the kitchen takeover serving delicious wings and hot dogs to Stirchley residents and visitors from across Brum and beyond.

Born from an 8 year passion project in which owner, Ted, began by serving wings in his back garden to family and friends, this kitchen residency has been a long time in the making and is filled with a love for tasty food bringing people together.

Having been inspired by the unusual flavours of wings that the team from The Butcher’s Social (who remembers that blast from the past?) used to serve, and having experimented with his own unique flavour combinations, Ted’s Wings was born. Living with a vegetarian who didn’t like him to fry chicken in the house, Ted built his very own fried chicken kitchen in the garden so he could indulge his newfound passion for outrageously flavoured wings.

After several prompts from loved ones who kept encouraging him to step out and do this for a living, Ted took the plunge and set up Ted’s Wings. And now, a few years down the line (where Ted’s Wings have become a firm fave of foodies in the know), he’s adding a whole new element to his offering – hot dogs! Ted’s Wings & Dogs now offers all of their wild and wonderful wings, but also tasty American style ‘dogs’.

Tucked away inside the ace local bar, Stir, Ted’s Wings & Dogs are serving up their tasty wings and dogs from their outdoor kitchen, complete with a brand new menu. If you’re in the mood for some fun and exciting wings then this is definitely the place, and flavours you can enjoy might include Cherry Cola, Salted Caramel (yum!), Dr Jalapeño Pepper, and Bacon, Pecan & Maple (incredible!).

The perfect snack to enjoy with a tasty drink from Stir, these wings have been building up a serious reputation. So if you’re in the market for some seriously good wings, then make sure to stop by and check them out for yourself. Plus, now that they’ve introduced their new ‘dogs’ to the menu, there’s even more deliciousness to choose from.

Made using premium ingredients, these are gourmet hot dogs like no other. With the likes of Spicy Calabrian Sausages and Wagyu Sausages on the menu, and piled high with mouth-watering toppings, these dogs are indulgent, delicious and a must try for all foodies out there. Make sure you go try these for yourself, they’re unmissable.

Life’s too short for boring wings, so make sure to head down to Ted’s Wings & Dogs to get your fix of fun flavours. Foodie glory awaits!

Now offering Independent Birmingham App members: 50% off wings (Tuesday – Thursday, before 8pm) + a FREE kid’s meal with a paying adult (Tuesday – Friday, 5pm – 7pm) OR 10% off food (anytime)

content.rendered:
It might sound cheesy but this place is un-brie-lievable.

Fresh off the back of a wonderful refurbishment, this fantastic independent has re-opened and they’re dialling up the flavour to new heights, with cheese boards from open to close.

Introducing Cheddar.

Located on Pershore Road, Stirchley, Cheddar is the cheese and wine bar bringing people together over a glass and a board.

We could ‘wheel’ out some tired old cheese puns about what a ‘grate’ time you’ll have at this cheese and wine bar, but we’re better than that… Ok, we’re not really but you’ve probably heard all of the cheesy puns before. So, instead we’ll just tell you all about how awesome Cheddar is and why you need to visit.

As the name would suggest, this place is all about the cheese (and the wine, don’t forget the wine!). Is there anything more delightfully indulgent than sitting down with an excellent glass of wine and a selection of mouth-watering cheeses and spending the evening grazing and sipping whilst you put the world to rights with your pals? We think not. To us, it’s the perfect way to spend an evening (or afternoon, or heck an entire day if you have enough cheese). That’s exactly what you can do at this ace bar in Stirchley.

Let’s talk cheese! That’s right, we’re getting straight to the good stuff. At Cheddar they expertly hand-pick the finest selection of cheeses from the UK and Europe for your eating pleasure. Then you just need to choose what size board to order (but the answer is always the biggest) and await your delicious selection of the finest cheeses. Simple. Easy. No fuss. All the cheese. Your cheeses will come with a selection of accompaniments (quince, capers, grapes, apples, crackers etc) and if you’re not feeling cheesy you can always just order some olives or almonds to nibble on instead.

The wine list at Cheddar is carefully curated to provide a thoughtfully chosen selection of reds, whites, roses, orange wine and Pet Nat – but the list is short and sweet. You won’t find pages and pages of choices which is great for those who are frozen by indecision and find an extensive list leaves them feeling completely overwhelmed by choice. Instead, there’s a hand-picked selection of artisan wines with something for everyone to enjoy, and if you need some help and advice choosing the perfect wine the friendly staff are on hand to provide guidance. If you’re not a wine fan, there are a selection of other drinks to choose from too, including craft beer and soft drinks.

In the biggest plot twist since The Red Wedding (IYKYK) Cheddar are introducing something new and exciting for their reopening too – the awesome BA-HA will be taking over the kitchen Monday – Thursday, offering a menu of mouth-watering, plant-based small plates (which will be available alongside the cheeseboards too). Perfect for sharing, you can mix and match, throw in a cheeseboard or stick to your favourites – it’s up to you! But with the likes of Miso Butter Corn Ribs, Truffle Polenta Fries, Shiitake Skewers, Rosé Pickled Beetroot and more – you’re going to want to try these small plates.

On top of all of this, on occasion you can shop for your own cheeses too. Once a month, the front of the store can be opened up to form the perfect cheese-shopping counter for your perusal. Stock up on your favourite cheeses and enjoy them in the comfort of your own home (or gift them to a cheese-loving friend).

The interior of the bar is decidedly dive bar-esque with low lighting, dark walls and tables, and a moody vibe. The red lighting gives the place a certain ‘je ne sais quoi’ and a cosy feel in the evenings, whilst the natural light from the windows makes this a cool place for a drink in daylight hours. You can send them a DM on Instagram to book (recommended for weekends) but walk-ins are welcome too. As they like to say – they take their cheese seriously, they take their wine seriously but they don’t take themselves too seriously.

If you love cheese and wine, or simply fancy another watering hole to choose from, then this little bar is a great place to frequent.

Now offering Independent Birmingham Members: 15% off food and drink (Monday – Thursday, 5pm – 7pm) + 10% off cheeseboards and house red/white wine (anytime)

content.rendered:
Birmingham’s craft beer scene is just going from strength to strength, and it’s a glorious thing to behold when one of Brum’s finest indies proves so popular that they’re able to expand their dreams further and add another fabulous venue to their roster.

Introducing The Barrel Store.

Located on Water Street in the Jewellery Quarter, The Barrel Store is a bar and barrel-ageing facility from the awesome team behind Brum’s beloved Attic Brew Co.

There’s nothing quite like enjoying a product at the site where it’s made, and this is precisely what you can do at this fantastic JQ-based independent. Sit amongst the barrels and enjoy one of Attic Brew Co.’s amazing beers right at their origin. As well as the delicious beers that are aged on-site, you can enjoy all of Attic’s other well-loved beers too, so you really are spoilt for choice.

Naturally, the main focus at The Barrel Store (the sister venue to Stirchley’s Attic Brew Co.) is amazing beers. The venue boasts 16 taps filled with fresh-as-you-can-get beers brewed at their HQ in Stirchley with lots of great options available no matter what your tastes are. All of their beers are vegan (and all of their food menu can be made vegan too). For the non-beer drinkers out there they also offer an array of wines, spirits, shooters, cocktails and low/no alcohol drinks too, thus catering for everyone.

At The Barrel Store they have a small kitchen, which, as of 4 April, is occupied by the ace Deathrow Pizza. From the team behind Deathrow Sandwich, this new pizza concept allows you to fully customise your pizza (choose your base, sauce, cheese and toppings) to create your ultimate pizza. With loads of different options to choose from you can create your very own dream pizza (the one you’d choose if it was your ‘last meal’) and all for a fixed price no matter what toppings you choose! We love this idea.

Community and inclusivity are at the heart of Attic Brew Co’s aims for The Barrel Store, so they proudly support a host of other fabulous local independents including Wine Freedom, Odi + Moo, Yorks Coffee, The Tiny Door Bookstore, The Book Club JQ and more, to provide a truly wonderful and varied local offering.

As well as being a wonderful place to enjoy a pint and a pizza, The Barrel Store are keen to be a big part of the local community, hosting regular events such as quiz nights, sports showings, games nights, speed dating and comedy shows to bring people together. These friendly and intimate events are a great way to get out there and have some fun whilst also supporting this brilliant independent business.

The interior at The Barrel Store is full of industrial vibes, with a minimalist look featuring metal beams, concrete floors and a neutral colour palette. The barrels and brewing equipment provide a focal point in this warehouse-style venue, nestled under the iconic railway arches of The Jewellery Quarter. The perfect mix of cosy yet airy, this is a fun and cool place to hang out whilst drinking some tasty beers and devouring a pizza or two.

Now offering Independent Birmingham App Members: A FREE pint of core Attic Brew Co beer when you purchase a pizza

content.rendered:
Some foods come and go like the seasons. Trends change, tastes change, and we move on. But pizza is eternal. Pizza never goes out of style.

Introducing Smoke + Ash.

Located on Greenfield Crescent in Edgbaston, Smoke + Ash is the pizzeria bringing the fire and the flavour to Birmingham’s suburbs.

If you’re anything like us, you love pizza. We just can’t get enough of the stuff. There’s never a bad time for pizza. It always satisfies your hunger, and it always puts a smile on your face. So when we heard of another amazing pizza place opening in Birmingham, we did a little happy dance. Smoke + Ash is the pizzeria making all of your dreams come true. Their focus is on Neapolitan pizzas done well, along with quality wines and seasonal twists on classic cocktails. A winning combination, if you ask us.

Their menu features a selection of Neapolitan style pizzas, using classic flavour combinations (because they’re classic for a reason). From Marinara and Margherita (our personal favourite, always), to salami (and fresh red chilli), prosciutto (with parmesan shavings and rocket), and goat’s cheese (with fig and balsamic syrup on a white base) – there’s something for everyone! They offer a selection of vegan options too, and the option to add a whole burrata to any pizza (yes, please). If you fancy an alternative to pizzas (or something to go with your pizza) they also offer a selection of sharing boards (charcuterie, cheese, or both) and sides (garlic bread, rocket salad, sundried tomatoes, or olives).

On top of the regulars, Smoke + Ash also offer a weekly special using some of the best seasonal ingredients and deliciously indulgent flavour combinations. As the special changes so regularly, if you spot one you like the sound of (which is basically all of them, right?) then you’d better hot-foot it down to Edgbaston to get your hands on one! Some examples of previous specials include: bresaola, spring onion and goat’s cheese; stilton, mortadella and garlic mushroom; and king prawns, spianata piccante (spicy sausage) and sweet chilli.

If you fancy something sweet after your pizza-based feast, Smoke + Ash have partnered up with some other fantastic local independent suppliers to offer you some delicious sweet treats: Odi + Moo ice cream, Tutto Apposto cannoli or tiramisu, and Quarter Horse coffee to go with them. Delicious!

You’ll need some drinks to go with all that food, and there are some fantastic choices on their menu. Their cocktail menu is full of classics with a Smoke + Ash twist (think Raspberry Clover Club, Chilli + Yuzu Margarita, Sloe Gin Negroni, and lots more). These delicious drinks are highly sippable, and we’re pretty sure you’ll want to make your way through the entire menu. If cocktails aren’t your thing though, they have lots of other options from quality wines to soft drinks (and tea, coffee, and hot chocolate if you fancy a hot drink instead).

The interior of the restaurant is modern and laid-back but with a luxe twist – the kind of place you’d be equally comfortable on a celebratory date night as you would just grabbing a quick, casual lunch. Plus, in absolutely game changing news, Smoke + Ash have also just opened a brand new outdoor terrace for your sunny day al fresco dining needs. If there’s one thing that makes incredible pizzas better, it’s eating them in the glorious sunshine. In fact, we can’t think of anything better than sitting in the sunshine, stuffing our faces with pizza and sipping on cocktails. Thank you Smoke + Ash for making our summer dreams come true.

Pro Tip: if you’re looking for a delicious lunchtime treat but don’t fancy a whole pizza, then we suggest you tuck into Smoke + Ash’s glorious panuozzi (plural of panuozzo, which is basically outrageously delicious sandwiches made using pizza dough). They come in 6 flavours and quite frankly you need to try them all. Forza Smoke + Ash!

So if you have those pizza cravings, head down to Edgbaston right now to satisfy them at the brilliant Smoke + Ash.

Now offering Independent Birmingham Members: 2 pizzas + 2 drinks (glass of house wine/pint of draught beer/spritz) + 2 mini desserts for £35 (Wednesday – Thursday) or 10% off the bill (anytime) or 20% off takeaways (collection only)

content.rendered:
If you live and work in Birmingham, it would have to be some miracle by which you haven’t heard of this particular restaurant. Reputations don’t come much bigger than this…

Introducing The Wilderness.

Photo Credit: Tom Bird

Located off Warstone Lane in the Jewellery Quarter, The Wilderness is the rock ‘n’ roll fine-dining restaurant with an attitude as big and bold as the flavours they serve.

Since they burst onto the scene with Chef Patron Alex Claridge at the helm, this unique restaurant has been making waves on the Birmingham dining scene and beyond. Thanks to Alex’s outspoken nature, the restaurant garnered a certain level of notoriety across the city, but it’s due to the incredible level of clever cookery and tantalising menus that they’ve remained a firm fixture on Brum’s best restaurants lists and continue to do so to this day.

The menus at The Wilderness are fine-dining in style (think tasting menus and a series of big flavours in small courses) but unlike anything else you will taste in the city. There’s a certain edginess to this rock ‘n’ roll restaurant, and a distinct lack of the pretentiousness that can sometimes haunt fine dining establishments.

At The Wilderness they serve provocative and playful tasting menus which change regularly as they’re built around the best produce available each week. Choose from the 6- or 10-course menus (we always recommend the 10-course for the ultimate foodie experience, but both are excellent) and expect quality ingredients prepared and served in bold and creative ways. This is a truly tantalising treat for your tastebuds.

Alongside the creative and exciting food menus, The Wilderness has a drinks list that perfectly compliments the bold flavours and creative flair showcased by the talented team of chefs. Whilst the optimal way to enjoy your tasting menu is with the accompanying drinks flight, you can, of course, opt for your own choice of beverage too. The drinks list at The Wilderness is all about top quality but also the unexpected. You’ll find fine wines from around the world, curated by their sommelier Sonal Clare (GQ Sommelier of the Year ’18, #9 Top 100 UK Sommeliers 2023), as well as an eclectic list of sake, spirits, cocktails and 0% ABV libations.

For those who have dined at this brilliant restaurant before, it will come as no surprise that they are long-standing holders of 3 AA Rosettes (one of the highest foodie accolades around) and have been awarded a number of other titles and recognitions over the years too (Harden’s Top 100, Squaremeal Top 100, Good Food Guide #10 Most Exciting Restaurants in the UK). They’re repeatedly named as one of Birmingham’s (and the UK’s) most exciting restaurants, and with very good reason. If there are any foodies out there who have yet to dine here, this is your sign to get booking that table immediately, and if you think fine dining isn’t for you, this restaurant might just change your mind…

Photo Credit: Tom Bird

The setting for this edgy eatery is that of a restored factory in the historic Jewellery Quarter and it couldn’t be more perfect. With just a handful of tables (and a tiny kitchen – where the chefs create what can only be described as miraculous plates of food, especially given the restrictive space) this is an intimate setting for a wonderfully memorable meal. Whether a special occasion or just a great Wednesday night, this is the perfect setting to create some foodie memories to last a lifetime. Set to the soundtrack of rock, punk and heavy metal, and with a colour palette of black, black, and more black (timeless, classic and seriously cool), this is a restaurant that is very comfortable with who it is, and makes no excuses for their punk reputation.

A small restaurant doing huge things, The Wilderness is an utter triumph and an essential ‘must visit’ dining experience for all true foodies. Book a table, wait in eager anticipation, then enter The Wilderness.

Now offering Independent Birmingham Members: 10% off the Tasting Menu (Wednesday – Thursday, excluding supplements and special event menus – valid for up to 2 people)

Important Booking Info

Bookings must be made directly with The Wilderness team by emailing: reservations@wearethewilderness.co.uk (stating you have a valid Independent Birmingham App, which you will be asked to present upon arrival in order to redeem the offer).

This offer only applies to the long tasting menu only, and excludes drinks and any additional supplements.

content.rendered:
Surprising, delightful, stimulating.

This is fine dining with a difference.

Introducing Opheem.

Located on Summer Row (Jewellery Quarter), Opheem is the two Michelin-starred restaurant from highly-celebrated chef Aktar Islam, bringing a taste of Indian fine dining to Birmingham.

In a sea of modern British restaurants, Opheem shines like a rare pearl in the ocean. Aktar Islam has brought together his signature style of cooking and a taste of his Indian heritage and created an incredible dining experience that will leave you invigorated, satisfied and wanting to return for more.

Constantly striving to push the boundaries of Indian flavours, and incorporating cooking techniques, both traditional and modern, from all over the world, this fantastic restaurant and the culinary delights served here are an insight into the inner working’s of Aktar’s mind.

At Opheem you can expect course after course of tempting and delicious dishes, each one as beautiful and delicious as the last and leaving you excited for the next plate to arrive at your table so you can discover the next step on this mouth-watering culinary journey. Naturally, the very best ingredients are used to create each flavour sensation, and each dish is cooked with precision and care by the talented team of chefs.

The menu changes regularly to keep things fresh, but you can always expect a powerful flavour punch in every course – and expect nothing less than to dine on some of the very best dishes you can eat in Birmingham. Choose between a 5- or 10-course tasting adventure (we recommend the 10-course to get the full experience and trust us – you’ll be glad you chose the 10-course menu when each dish arrives and you taste smash hit after smash hit), and savour each incredible mouthful of every colourful and insanely beautiful dish that arrives at your table.

The restaurant space itself is among the most sophisticated in the city. From the beautiful lounge area where you can enjoy a welcome snack and drink, to the stunning dining room with accents of grey and gold (not to mention some seriously cool light fittings), providing a modern and elegant dining space in which to enjoy your foodie experience in comfort, the interiors compliment the style and quality of food perfectly. Best of all, you can see into the kitchen too – so you can see the masterful chefs at work as they create the stunning dishes you’re about to eat.

In addition to exquisite dishes, both in taste and appearance, Opheem also has a cracking wine list and a carefully-curated cocktail menu featuring a whole bunch of dangerously drinkable mixed drinks – all with a heavy chef’s influence, using seasonal ingredients, high quality produce, and constantly evolving alongside their food menu. Short but focused, the mixed drinks list is all about providing the best drinks alongside the best food, whether its pre-, post- or during your dinner.

Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or simply want to enjoy an amazing and unmissable foodie experience, this restaurant is sublime. To match the amazing food, the service is warm and welcoming, and you will feel at ease as soon as you step through the door.

If you’re looking for a fine dining experience like no other in Birmingham, you must book a table at Opheem, the city’s first two Michelin-starred restaurant.

content.rendered:
If there’s one thing that we can’t live without, it’s pizza.

Pizza is the answer to all of life’s big questions. What should I eat for dinner? Pizza. What will make me feel better? Pizza. How should I celebrate? Pizza! There’s no situation that can’t be improved by a truly great pizza. And if you’re on the lookout for a truly great pizzeria, we have just the place.

Introducing Alicia’s Micro Bakehouse.

Located on Pershore Road, Stirchley, Alicia’s Micro Bakehouse is the micro pizzeria doing mighty things.

The principles of making pizza are fairly simple, but making truly exceptional pizzas is an art. At Alicia’s Micro Bakehouse they specialise in 100% sourdough fermented Neapolitan style pizzas, and their passion for incredible pizzas is poured into them at every step of the process.

The best pizzas start with the best base and Alicia’s have perfected their sourdough pizza dough to ensure the very best flavour and texture for every single pizza. To create the very best pizzas, they are all baked in a 100% wood fired oven for that deliciously smoky flavour and perfect crust.

The menu at Alicia’s is filled with crowd-pleasing favourites as well as seasonal specials, tasty starters and sides for when you fancy a little something extra, and tempting desserts to satisfy your sweet tooth. They even have a kids ‘Bambini’ pizza option so the little ones can enjoy the same great taste but with a smaller portion (and a choice of topping).

Enjoy a selection of Italian starters and sides such as arancini, garlic bread, caprese salad and more to accompany your pizzas. For the main event you can choose from a range of truly delicious toppings, from the classic Margherita to Spicy Meat, Alicia’s Napoletana and more adventurous options like the Noci (pomodoro, mozzarella, Parmigiano Reggiano, gorgonzola picante, walnuts, caramelised onion) and rotating seasonal specials. You can even add extra toppings to your chosen pizza if you wish to fully customise your choice to your tastes.

To finish your delicious Italian feast, make sure to save room for one of their delightful desserts. Whether you go for their decadent take on an Affogato, the traditional Torta Della Nonna (Grandma’s Cake – a classic Tuscan dessert made from rich pastry, custard and toasted nuts, served with a scoop of gelato of choice), Sicilian Cannoli, or a simple scoop of gelato – there’s something for everyone to enjoy.

To accompany your feast there’s a great selection of drinks available to choose, from classic cocktails to spritzes and aperitifs, or hand-selected Italian wines, to Italian beers, a selection of soft drinks and teas and coffees too. Whatever you’re in the mood for, there’s a drink for you. Plus, every Saturday at Alicia’s, you can enjoy a delicious bottomless brunch, perfect for when you need a catch up with your pals. Enjoy a starter and main or a main and dessert for just £35pp, including bottomless Prosecco.

The space itself is cosy and welcoming, the perfect place for enjoying a beautiful pizza with loved ones, and they have a glorious little garden out back too. Sitting in the garden when the weather is warm, enjoying your pizza al fresco is truly unmatched. You can also order their mouth-watering pizzas for delivery too – perfect for when you can’t be bothered to leave the house.

So the next time those pizza cravings hit, you know exactly where to go – because a trip to Alicia’s Micro Bakehouse is guaranteed to be packed with incredible flavour.

content.rendered:
One of the many things we love about our fair city is the plethora of incredible street food traders.

Another, is when said street food traders find such success that they open their very own restaurants in Brum. As one of the pioneers of Brum’s booming street food scene and one of the city’s favourite traders, when this particular restaurant opened, the city as a whole did a little happy dance. And then booked themselves a table…

Introducing Soi 1268.

Located on Pershore Road, Stirchley, Soi 1268 is the bricks and mortar restaurant giving one of Brum’s most beloved street food traders a permanent home in the city (and your new favourite place to eat).

This independent will likely need no introduction for many of you, but in case you’ve been living under a rock (or, you know, just moved to the city) one of Brum’s best loved street food traders, Buddha Belly, opened Soi 1268 in 2023 as a permanent home for their delicious Thai street eats. And we, like the rest of the good folk of Brum, were absolutely thrilled.

Owners Sai and James met in 2004 and bonded over their love of food. In 2012, James encouraged Sai to enter Masterchef where out of 20,000 applicants Sai made it to the final 24. The competition gave her the confidence to pursue her love of cooking and begin a career in the food industry. Using everything she’d learned about Thai food from her mother, she began to develop her family’s secret recipes.

At Soi 1268 you can find all of the incredible Thai eats that you’ve come to love from Buddha Belly, as well as some extra special dishes too. All made from authentic ingredients and recipes passed down through Sai’s family, these mouth-watering dishes are truly some of the best you will eat in Birmingham.

The menu features a combination of tasty Thai small plates along with their famous street food bowls. From their incredible Thai Fried Chicken to their ultimate King Prawn Toast (the best prawn toast we’ve ever had the pleasure of devouring), the small plates are packed full of flavour. In fact, you might as well just order one of everything.

For the main event, there are a number of options to choose from, each as deep in flavour and dangerously moreish as the last. From rich and indulgent, heart-warming Beef Massaman to spicy Chicken Panang and, of course, their Thai Fried Chicken bowl (a Buddha Belly classic) there are loads of delicious dishes for you to sink your teeth into. Vegan options are available too, as well as gluten-free options and kids meals for the little ones.

The drinks list is composed of a carefully curated selection of beers, wines, spirits, and soft drinks, as well as a house cocktail option too – so there really is something for everyone to enjoy.

The restaurant itself is cosy and laid-back with industrial inspired décor (think wooden tables, exposed lightbulbs, corrugated metal and a moody colour palette). The perfect crossover between their street food roots and a relaxed restaurant space, this is the ideal place to enjoy some delicious Thai food.

If by some miracle you’ve yet to set foot in this foodie paradise, may we suggest (or politely demand) that you book yourself a table immediately. And if you have already been, this is your sign to go again! This truly is some of the best food you’ll eat in Brum. We’ll see you there…

content.rendered:
Step into this family-run restaurant for a taste of Iranian cuisine, stay for the heart-felt welcome.

Introducing Colbeh.

Located on Hagley Road, Colbeh is the Persian restaurant where you’re welcomed in like family.

Fresh off the back of a stunning refurbishment, Colbeh have flung open their doors once again and are ready and waiting to welcome you back in for a taste of their mouth-watering dishes. The space is looking stunning, the new menu is packed full of incredible flavours, and the hospitality is as warm and friendly as ever.

Along with the décor, the Colbeh team have updated the menu too. The new menu is packed full of mouth-watering dishes, giving an authentic taste of Persian cuisine, with dishes representing each of the different regions of Iran. Using traditional family recipes to represent one of the world’s most ancient styles of cooking, you’ll find everything from fragrant rice, slow cooked stews, fragrant fresh herbs, perfectly seasoned meats and more, all packed full of flavours and spices.

The new menu features a selection of both hot and cold small plates which are perfect for sharing, or to get a taste of lots of different dishes. Alongside the small plates, you can also enjoy House Grill dishes (think mouth-watering grilled meats with a choice of side), and traditional dishes like Stew of the Day, Baghali Polo Ba Ghosht (slow-cooked cut of lamb on the bone, broad beans and dill rice), and lots more.

If you have a sweet tooth, then you must try one of their decadent and down-right delicious desserts. From delicious ice creams (think chocolate and hazelnut, or saffron-infused ice cream with pistachios) to Affogato, and mouth-watering Baklava. If you can’t decide between Baklava and ice cream then go for their delicious combination of both – an ice cream sandwich of Baklava and saffron-infused ice cream, the perfect combination.

To make sure the drinks are just as delicious as the food, the team have been taste testing and recipe developing behind the scenes, to ensure that all of their cocktails are in tip top shape. Whether you like something sweet and fruity or something short and sharp, they have a drink for everyone. Of course, there are plenty of other drinks on the menu too if you’re not a fan of cocktails, so don’t worry you’ll find something tasty to sip on while you tuck into your delicious food, whether that’s a glass of wine, a crisp, cold beer, or a refreshing soft drink. They also offer tea and coffee, including infused Persian teas.

The name ‘Colbeh’ means cottage in the Persian language of Farsi, and every detail at this beautiful restaurant has been hand-picked to give that welcoming, cosy feeling of stepping into a family home. From the hanging lanterns offering up a soft, warm glow, to the traditional rugs lining the floor, the arched mirrors and intricate embroidery adorning the handmade decorations, there are so many thoughtful details. The interior is beautiful and the perfect mix of luxe and cosy, making the space perfect for any occasion, big or small.

If you’re looking for the perfect place for a special celebration, they also have a private dining room – so you can celebrate in style, in your own beautiful space with delicious food. What’s not to love?

If you’re yet to visit Colbeh, then make sure to right that wrong immediately and visit this fantastic independent restaurant, full of heart and soul (and delicious food!).

content.rendered:
If you’re a foodie in Birmingham, then these guys need no introduction, but indulge us anyway.

Legends of the foodie scene, from street food to bricks and mortar, the purveyors of filth…

Introducing Original Patty Men.

Located on Shaw’s Passage, Digbeth, Original Patty Men is where you go when your burger cravings strike, and only the best will do.

It’s tough these days for independent businesses to remain open, so it truly is remarkable when places have been open for a decade or more, and a true testament to the quality of their offering. Enter Original Patty Men (O.P.M.) who have been on the scene for over ten years, and aren’t going anywhere anytime soon.

Having quit their previous jobs, Tom and Scott (founders of O.P.M.) were on a mission to create a truly epic independent burger in Brum, back when they were pretty hard to find. Having burst onto the street food scene, taking the early Digbeth Dining Club days by storm and building up a strong reputation for slinging out the best burgs in town (and thanks to * that * iconic Krispy Kreme burger – IYKYK), they took the big step of opening their very own burger joint, whilst still maintaining a strong presence on the street food circuit.

Their Digbeth based burger restaurant is found on Shaw’s Passage, tucked away under the railway arches behind Moor Street Station, and is home to some of the very best burgs in Brum. If by some miracle you still haven’t paid them a visit, then that needs to be rectified immediately. Once you go O.P.M. there’s no going back.

On the menu at this ace restaurant are their signature burgers (and of course some tasty specials), mouth-watering sides and a dessert or two. All of their burgers are made fresh using high quality ingredients, and their signature Aged Longhorn Beef Patties make these some of the tastiest burgers around.

Their seriously naughty burgers are the thing of dreams and there are several options to choose from, plus regularly changing specials too. Go for a classic flavour like the Cheezy-E (aged longhorn beef patty, American cheese, lettuce, white onion, pickle and Boss Man sauce) or the Bacon Cheese (aged longhorn beef patty, streaky bacon, American cheese, lettuce, red onion, pickle, ketchup, and American mustard), or go for the Pineapple Express ( aged longhorn beef patty, cheddar cheese, streaky bacon, lettuce, red jalapeno, tomato and pineapple hot sauce) or the Alabama Slammer (deep fried boneless chicken thigh, lime and ginger slaw and a choice of Alabama sauce or Frank’s hot sauce).

There are some tasty veggie and vegan options on the menu too including The Vegan One featuring a fried tofu patty and sriracha hot sauce or the Po Money Po Mushroom – a panko breaded mushroom Po’boy style sandwich. If you fancy something extra on the sides there’s house slaw, boneless nugz (deep fried chicken nuggets), a great choice of fries either naked or loaded with tasty toppings, and they have a selection of tasty chicken wings too (BBQ, Alabama, or Buffalo).

The restaurant itself is stripped back and industrial, a great casual place to enjoy some tasty burgers. You’ll catch their signature cartoon branding dotted around, and there’s plenty of seating at the wooden tables. If there’s a short wait for a table when you arrive, you can join the list and pop next door to their bar Kilder to enjoy a drink while you wait.

If you’re somehow yet to visit this legendary burger joint, or if you’re just well overdue a return trip (or even if you went there yesterday) – consider this your reminder to go and gobble up some tasty burgers by the best.

content.rendered:
Small plates are having a big moment, and we love it.

How often have you looked at a menu and wished you could try a little bit of just about every dish you read? Tapas and small plates give you a chance to do just that – sample a little bit of lots of different dishes. That’s what we love about this style of dining (and why it’s such a popular way to eat these days).

Introducing Plates By Purnell’s.

Located on Edmund Street (just around the corner from the brilliant Michelin starred Purnell’s Restaurant), Plates By Purnell’s is the tapas restaurant bringing a slice of the Spanish sunshine to Brum.

When you hear that one of Brum’s favourite, most celebrated local chefs is opening a new venture with the same passion and ethos behind it as their flagship Michelin starred fine dining restaurant, but with a more relaxed style, you jump for joy. Or, at least, we do. When we first heard of the concept behind Plates By Purnell’s, we could not have been more excited. Filling a void in the market, this restaurant brings high end (but insanely affordable) tapas to Brum, and it’s just what we’ve been missing!

On the menu at Plates By Purnell’s are a range of small plates inspired by classic Spanish tapas. The menu is split into sections: “Pintxos” (Appetisers), “Verduras” (Vegetables), “Carnes” (Meat), “Pescado y Marisco” (Fish & Seafood) and “Postres” (Desserts) to make your ordering nice and simple. Everything on the menu is absolutely delicious, made using the best, authentic Spanish ingredients and cooked to perfection by the talented team of chefs – so whichever dishes you choose, you’ll be in for a real treat.

Featured on the menu are classics such as Pan Con Tomate (a simple sounding dish of tomato and olive oil on toasted bread, but it’s a classic – and really delicious), gloriously charred and salted Padron Peppers, deliciously crispy and oozy Cheese Croquettes, the Spanish classic potato dish Patatas Bravas, perfectly cooked Grilled Octopus and sizzling Prawns with Garlic, among lots of other delicious dishes. From one bite you’ll be in heaven and already wondering when you can come back for even more tasty tapas.

To accompany your Spanish feast, you’ll want to choose some equally tasty drinks. Lots of the drinks are traditionally Spanish, or excellent companions to the yummy tapas you’ll be scoffing – from everyone’s favourite, Sangria, to a strong compliment of sherries, and a selection of Spanish wines. There is of course a selection of beers, spirits, cocktails and soft drinks too, so whatever you fancy, there’s a drink for you.

This small and cosy restaurant is reminiscent of the little tapas bars found all over Spain. With deep wooden accents, Mediterranean style tiles and vibrant platewear, the décor is absolutely spot on and the perfect compliment to the delicious Spanish-inspired food. The extra details such as the greenery hanging from the ceiling and the paintings of bulls (a symbol iconic to both Spain and Birmingham) add the perfect finishing touches. You might be forgiven for thinking you’d stepped through a portal direct to Spain itself (although one look outside will remind you you’re in dear old Brum).

The perfect spot for your next date night, a casual dinner with friends, or a long leisurely lunch, get booking your table now and go enjoy the best tapas in the city.

content.rendered:
If you enjoy the delights of Mexican cuisine and you like to dine in a beautiful space, then we have just the place for you…

Introducing The Mayan.

Located in The Mailbox, The Mayan is the upmarket Mexican restaurant serving tasty eats in a swanky setting.

The Mayan is the restaurant where ancient Mayan flavours meet modern Mexican cuisine, bringing you a delicious taste of South America. Alongside their delicious food they specialise in Mezcal, and here you can enjoy some of the finest Mezcal around. Paying homage to the rich heritage of the Mayan civilisation, this fantastic restaurant offers a vibrant menu blending traditional ingredients with modern culinary techniques.

The menu at The Mayan draws on inspiration from across Mexico, showcasing a diverse range of flavours that define Mexican cuisine. From the hot, fiery spices of the Yucatan Peninsula to the exotic fruits and aromatic herbs, each dish tells a story and is sure to tantalise your tastebuds. With the full menu available in the evening, and a more condensed version available at lunch, The Mayan also serve a Mexican bottomless brunch. This brunch is a great alternative to the classic bottomless offerings and with different ‘tiers’ available (depending on how much food you want to eat and which drinks you’d like to choose from) is a great way to celebrate with pals.

The main food menu at The Mayan is full of mouth-watering Mexican flavours and authentic dishes reimagined. From delicious appetisers and starters (think guac and chips, frijoles, empanadas and more) to tasty tacos and fresh, zingy ceviche there are so many exciting ways to start off your dining experience. For the main event you can enjoy delicious meats from the grill (including premium cuts of British beef, lamb and chicken) elevated with vibrant Mexican spices and salsas, or choose one of their traditional Mexican recipes reinvented for the modern palate (think Carnitas, Barbacoa Lamb Shank, Pollo Con Mole and more).

For the sweet-toothed amongst you, The Mayan have a tantalising array of exquisite desserts to choose from to perfectly round off your experience. From the classic Churros to a refreshing Ensalada De Frutas or the decadent Choco Pinata, there’s something for everyone. If you’re too full for a dessert, try one of their Mayan Hot Chocolates instead – a traditional spicy hot chocolate made with milk, cinnamon and chilli.

In keeping with their Mexican theme, the drinks list features a wide range of authentic drinks, including many originating from Mexico. On the drinks list are a vast selection of fine wines, craft beers and premium spirits, alongside whisky from Oaxaca, rum from Puebla, gin from The Yucatan and a diverse selection of Tequila and Mezcal. For cocktail lovers, there’s also a list of handcrafted cocktails carefully designed to compliment the ambience and the dishes at The Mayan. These spectacular cocktails are designed to ignite all of the senses from the visual appearance to the scent and, of course, the taste. For those who prefer non-alocholic drinks, there’s an equally impressive list of carefully curated non-alcoholic cocktails that are just as delicious as their boozy counterparts too.

The interior at The Mayan is up-market and super swanky, with highly decadent touches to the décor making this a beautiful setting for a delicious meal. The focal point of the restaurant is a spectacular tree in the centre of the venue – reflecting the Mayan Ceiba Tree (a mythical tree in the centre of the universe connecting the underworld and human realms with the gods). The luxe seating features dark velvet chairs and bar stools with gold accented tables and a stunning bar with an impressive back-bar showcasing the wide range of mezcals on offer (quite possibly the largest collection in Brum, we hear). This is a truly spectacular venue for a special occasion or just a delightful mid-week date night or catch up. Whatever the occasion, delicious modern Mexican food and fancy cocktails are always a good idea.

content.rendered:
Step into a secret garden and discover this foodie paradise tucked away on a stunning rural estate just minutes away from Birmingham.

Sound too good to be true? Well, it isn’t! Set in the old furnace house of the walled garden at Hampton Manor’s sprawling foodie estate is a gorgeous restaurant offering unparalleled flavours, unmatched vibes and unbelievable satisfaction.

Introducing Kynd.

Located on the Hampton Manor Estate, Hampton-in-Arden, Kynd is the gorgeous produce-led restaurant making your foodie dreams come true.

If you’re familiar with the wonderful Hampton Manor estate then you’ll know that everything they do is with intention, from the interiors to the ingredients and everything in between. This new restaurant is no different. Run by Executive Chef David Taylor and his wife Anette, who also run the estate’s other incredible restaurant (the fabulous, Michelin-starred Grace & Savour), this produce-led, neighbourhood restaurant is putting out some truly mouth-watering plates of food, and we’re confident it will become one of your new favourite places to eat.

At Kynd, they’re all about taking the very best British produce and treating it with the respect and care it deserves, lovingly transforming high quality, seasonal ingredients into mouth-watering plates of food. They work closely with their hand-picked suppliers and farmers to ensure the very best dining experience for their customers. The menu changes regularly to reflect the best seasonal ingredients, but is always a carefully curated menu reflecting their casual yet considered approach to dining, and showcasing ingredients in their purest, simplest form while embracing the low-waste, farm-to-table ethos synonymous with the 45-acre estate.

Whilst the menus do change regularly, you will always have the option of a 3-course A La Carte menu (with optional snacks and cheese course) or a five-course ‘Taste of Kynd’ set menu. Whatever you choose, your tastebuds are in for a real treat with dishes such as Cornish Crab, Salted Turnip, Pickled Fennel or Hebridean Hand-Dived Scallops, Pumpkin, Organic Apple to start, Ex-Dairy Flat Iron, Black Garlic & Onion Miso Butter, Rainbow Chard or Cornish Skate Wing, Creamed Spinach, Wild Garlic Capers, Roasted Fish Bone Sauce for mains, and Ruby Hue 70% Chocolate Marquis, Creme Fraiche or Tispy Cake Soaked In Organic Welsh Rum, Brown Butter Ice Cream (to share) for dessert, you’re in for a truly memorable meal. All of the mains are served with a melt-in-your-mouth potato fondant to share (although we’re pretty sure you won’t want to), and Sunday lunch brings the option of a traditional Sunday roast too.

To complement the incredible food offering, the drinks list is just as well considered. Like the rest of their menus, the drinks list celebrates the revolution in sustainable farming practices. From low intervention wines (including wines on tap, providing quality and value by the carafe), to the UK’s first carbon-negative beer, the thoughtful selection of drinks reflects their ethos perfectly. If you prefer, they also offer cocktails and mocktails, garnished from their garden.

The interior at Kynd brings a relaxed yet sophisticated atmosphere with dark wood tables, chic pendant lights and leather seating all adding to the moody, cosy ambience. In the warmer months, recline in one of the beautiful greenhouses for al fresco dining amid the plants and vines and make the most of the sunshine. Whether you’re celebrating a momentous occasion or simply enjoying a delicious lunch with a loved one, this restaurant is the ideal place to enjoy the very best things in life: great food, great drinks and great company.

content.rendered:
Foodies, listen up – this one’s for you!

Hampton Manor are winning the game right now. The game being creating the ultimate foodie experiences. The estate is growing with each new addition adding to the offering, never detracting from what’s already there. Pushing the boundaries and creating something truly special – and with their latest addition, they’ve done it again.

Introducing Grace & Savour.

Located on the Hampton Manor estate, Grace & Savour is a fine dining foodie experience that will blow you away.

Hampton Manor just get it. Everything they do is incredible and each time they add a new experience or a new restaurant it draws us back in for another taste, each one a distinct experience in its own right but each one totally knocking our socks off. The latest addition to Hampton Manor’s foodie paradise is the sensational Grace & Savour, which has opened up to glowing reviews in the press (unsuprisingly – it’s fantastic!).

Nestled inside the stunning Victorian walled garden, this restaurant is the full package. The seriously stylish interiors matched perfectly by the sumptuous fifteen-course tasting menu. Overlooking the gorgeous kitchen gardens (where so much of the food you will eat is grown), the views are breathtaking. Whether you sit on one of the tables, bathed in natural light from the huge windows, or you choose a seat at the countertop that surrounds the open kitchen, you will be in for a foodie experience of a lifetime.

Head Chef David Taylor, born in the Midlands, learnt his craft right here in Birmingham (he was sous chef at the brilliant Purnell’s in his younger years), before becoming part of the team that won three Michelin stars at the legendary Maaemo in Norway. Returning to the UK to help create this incredible new dining experience, he’s bringing a wealth of knowledge, experience and ideas to showcase incredible produce and cooking techniques.

The menu is designed to celebrate the estate’s commitment to a progressive movement of farmers and growers who take pride in caring for the soil and the environment. Soil health, sustainability and biodiversity are key factors in the future of food, and David believes farming is the key to unlocking flavour. Making the most of the fabulous ingredients, the chefs are building up their stores, pickling and preserving to create a library to dip into at a later date.

Unsurprisingly the food is outstanding. Each course is as sensational and delightful to look at as it is to taste. The time spent sourcing suppliers and ingredients shows, as does the incredible talent of David and his team of chefs. The menu changes to reflect seasonality but it will always delight, intrigue, and satisfy.

Every detail at this stunning restaurant has been carefully thought out and considered: from the seriously sexy interiors (if you love design, thank us later), to the relaxing rooms, the like-minded suppliers and, of course, the delicious dishes and perfectly matched drinks (Wine Freedom are on the wine list, naturally – but you’ll also find other carefully selected alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, and a drinks pairing is available too). All of these considered details add up to create this wonderful, complete experience.

For the ultimate experience, an overnight stay is an absolute must. A few tables are reserved for non-residents, but when you see the stunning bedrooms (and to enjoy an incredible breakfast the next day), an overnight stay in the adjoining Timber Yard will be extremely tempting. Sympathetic to the former timber yard roots of the building, the bedrooms feature earthy palettes and textures, exposed wooden beams and possibly the most delicious bathtubs we’ve ever seen. With Harvest products in the bathroom (another Indy-B favourite), you can enjoy an indulgent and pampering stay to complete the relaxing and rejuvenating experience. Designed by Hampton Manor’s very own Fjona, these bedrooms are a luxurious experience in themselves.

If you’re looking for the perfect foodie getaway, a special treat for a loved one, or you’re just a massive foodie and love what Hampton Manor are doing (samesies!), then a trip to Grace & Savour is essential.
